when_to_say: Used as a general daytime greeting between people who are not close friends or family.
example: こんにちは、元気ですか？ (konnichiwa, genki desu ka?) - Hello, how are you?

when_to_say: Used casually in the morning with friends or family; add 'ございます' for politeness.
example: おはよう、よく眠れた？ (ohayou, yoku nemureta?) - Good morning, did you sleep well?

when_to_say: Used as a greeting after the sun goes down.
example: こんばんは、お仕事お疲れ様です。 (konbanwa, oshigoto otsukaresama desu.) - Good evening, thanks for your hard work today.

when_to_say: Used when parting for a long time; casual friends usually say something lighter like じゃあね.
example: さようなら、また来週。 (sayounara, mata raishuu.) - Goodbye, see you next week.

when_to_say: Used to express gratitude in informal settings; add ございます for politeness.
example: ありがとう、手伝ってくれて！ (arigatou, tetsudatte kurete!) - Thank you for helping me!

when_to_say: Used to apologize, get someone's attention, or say a polite 'excuse me'.
example: すみません、駅はどこですか？ (sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka?) - Excuse me, where is the station?

when_to_say: Used when counting items or stating the number one.
example: りんごが一つあります。 (ringo ga hitotsu arimasu.) - There is one apple.

when_to_say: Used when counting or referring to the number two.
example: 猫が二匹います。 (neko ga nihiki imasu.) - There are two cats.

when_to_say: Used when counting or referring to the number three.
example: 三時に会いましょう。 (sanji ni aimashou.) - Let's meet at three o'clock.

when_to_say: Used for counting; 'shi' is avoided in some contexts because it sounds like 'death'.
example: 四月に桜が咲きます。 (shigatsu ni sakura ga sakimasu.) - Cherry blossoms bloom in April.

when_to_say: Used when counting or stating the number five.
example: 五分待ってください。 (gofun matte kudasai.) - Please wait five minutes.

when_to_say: Used as the base counting unit for ten and multiples of ten.
example: 十時に出発します。 (juuji ni shuppatsu shimasu.) - We depart at ten o'clock.

when_to_say: Used when talking about your own or someone else's family as a group.
example: 私の家族は四人です。 (watashi no kazoku wa yonin desu.) - My family has four people.

when_to_say: Used to refer humbly to your own mother when speaking with others.
example: 母は料理が上手です。 (haha wa ryouri ga jouzu desu.) - My mother is good at cooking.

when_to_say: Used to refer humbly to your own father when speaking with others.
example: 父は毎朝走ります。 (chichi wa maiasa hashirimasu.) - My father runs every morning.

when_to_say: Used to ask about or describe one's siblings collectively.
example: 兄弟は何人いますか？ (kyoudai wa nan-nin imasu ka?) - How many siblings do you have?

when_to_say: Used casually to refer to a friend of any gender.
example: 彼は私の親友です。 (kare wa watashi no shinyuu desu.) - He is my best friend.

when_to_say: Used to refer to a child, either generally or one's own.
example: 子供が公園で遊んでいます。 (kodomo ga kouen de asonde imasu.) - The children are playing in the park.

when_to_say: Used when asking for or referring to drinking water.
example: 水を一杯ください。 (mizu wo ippai kudasai.) - Please give me a glass of water.

when_to_say: Used both for cooked rice and generally for a meal.
example: 朝ご飯を食べましたか？ (asagohan wo tabemashita ka?) - Did you eat breakfast?

when_to_say: Used when ordering or talking about the Japanese dish sushi.
example: 寿司が大好きです。 (sushi ga daisuki desu.) - I love sushi.

when_to_say: Used to compliment food that tastes good, often said while eating.
example: これはとても美味しいです。 (kore wa totemo oishii desu.) - This is very delicious.

when_to_say: Used to describe food that has a hot, spicy taste.
example: このカレーは辛いです。 (kono karee wa karai desu.) - This curry is spicy.

when_to_say: Used when offering or asking for green tea, common in daily life.
example: お茶を飲みませんか？ (ocha wo nomimasen ka?) - Would you like some tea?

when_to_say: Used to refer to the current day in conversation.
example: 今日は忙しいです。 (kyou wa isogashii desu.) - I am busy today.

when_to_say: Used to talk about plans or events happening the next day.
example: 明日、映画を見ます。 (ashita, eiga wo mimasu.) - I will watch a movie tomorrow.

when_to_say: Used to refer to the day before today.
example: 昨日は雨でした。 (kinou wa ame deshita.) - It rained yesterday.

when_to_say: Used when asking about duration or availability of time.
example: 時間がありますか？ (jikan ga arimasu ka?) - Do you have time?

when_to_say: Used when making plans for Saturday and Sunday.
example: 週末は何をしますか？ (shuumatsu wa nani wo shimasu ka?) - What will you do on the weekend?

when_to_say: Used to describe habitual actions that happen daily.
example: 毎日日本語を勉強します。 (mainichi nihongo wo benkyou shimasu.) - I study Japanese every day.

when_to_say: Used when giving directions or talking about train stations.
example: 駅まで歩いて行きます。 (eki made aruite ikimasu.) - I will walk to the station.

when_to_say: Used when discussing travel plans or arriving/departing by plane.
example: 空港まで送ってください。 (kuukou made okutte kudasai.) - Please take me to the airport.

when_to_say: Used when buying or referring to a train, bus, or event ticket.
example: 切符を二枚ください。 (kippu wo nimai kudasai.) - Two tickets, please.

when_to_say: Used when asking for or giving directions.
example: この道をまっすぐ行ってください。 (kono michi wo massugu itte kudasai.) - Please go straight on this road.

when_to_say: Used when navigating or asking for a map of an area.
example: 地図を見せてください。 (chizu wo misete kudasai.) - Please show me the map.

when_to_say: Used when talking about taking a trip somewhere.
example: 来月、旅行に行きます。 (raigetsu, ryokou ni ikimasu.) - I will go on a trip next month.

when_to_say: Used as the basic verb for eating food.
example: 朝ご飯を食べます。 (asagohan wo tabemasu.) - I eat breakfast.

when_to_say: Used as the basic verb for drinking liquids.
example: 水を飲みます。 (mizu wo nomimasu.) - I drink water.

when_to_say: Used to describe movement toward a place.
example: 学校に行きます。 (gakkou ni ikimasu.) - I go to school.

when_to_say: Used to describe movement toward the speaker.
example: 友達が家に来ます。 (tomodachi ga ie ni kimasu.) - My friend is coming to my house.

when_to_say: Used for watching something like TV or looking at something.
example: 映画を見ます。 (eiga wo mimasu.) - I watch a movie.

when_to_say: Used when talking about speaking a language or having a conversation.
example: 日本語を話します。 (nihongo wo hanashimasu.) - I speak Japanese.

when_to_say: Used to describe an activity or event that is enjoyable.
example: 旅行はとても楽しいです。 (ryokou wa totemo tanoshii desu.) - The trip is very fun.

when_to_say: Used to express personal happiness about something that happened.
example: 会えて嬉しいです。 (aete ureshii desu.) - I'm happy to meet you.

when_to_say: Used to describe feeling sorrow or unhappiness.
example: 彼女は悲しい顔をしていました。 (kanojo wa kanashii kao wo shite imashita.) - She had a sad face.

when_to_say: Used to describe something frightening or a fearful feeling.
example: このホラー映画は怖いです。 (kono horaa eiga wa kowai desu.) - This horror movie is scary.

when_to_say: Used to say you feel physically or mentally exhausted.
example: 今日はとても疲れました。 (kyou wa totemo tsukaremashita.) - I am very tired today.

when_to_say: Used to reassure someone or ask if something is alright.
example: 大丈夫ですか？ (daijoubu desu ka?) - Are you okay?

when_to_say: Used when talking about a shop or business location.
example: このお店は安いです。 (kono omise wa yasui desu.) - This shop is cheap.

when_to_say: Used when asking about or discussing the cost of an item.
example: 値段はいくらですか？ (nedan wa ikura desu ka?) - How much is the price?

when_to_say: Used to describe something with a low, affordable price.
example: この服は安いです。 (kono fuku wa yasui desu.) - These clothes are cheap.

when_to_say: Used to describe something costly, or physically tall.
example: このバッグは高いです。 (kono baggu wa takai desu.) - This bag is expensive.

when_to_say: Used as the basic verb for purchasing something.
example: 新しい靴を買いました。 (atarashii kutsu wo kaimashita.) - I bought new shoes.

when_to_say: Used generally when talking about money or cash.
example: お金がありません。 (okane ga arimasen.) - I don't have money.

when_to_say: Used to encourage someone before a challenge or effort.
example: 試験、頑張ってね！ (shiken, ganbatte ne!) - Good luck on your exam!

when_to_say: Used to congratulate someone on an achievement or celebration.
example: 合格おめでとう！ (goukaku omedetou!) - Congratulations on passing!

when_to_say: Used among coworkers at the end of a task or workday.
example: お疲れ様でした。 (otsukaresama deshita.) - Thank you for your hard work today.

meaning: thank you for the meal (before eating)
when_to_say: Said before starting to eat to express gratitude for the meal.
example: いただきます！ (itadakimasu!) - Let's eat! (lit. I gratefully receive)

meaning: thank you for the meal (after eating)
when_to_say: Said after finishing a meal to thank whoever prepared it.
example: ごちそうさまでした。 (gochisousama deshita.) - Thank you for the meal.

when_to_say: Used casually when parting, implying you'll meet again another time.
example: じゃあ、また今度ね。 (jaa, mata kondo ne.) - Well then, see you next time.
